title: Expediting Higher Fidelity Plasma State Reconstructions for the DIII-D National Fusion Facility Using Leadership Class Computing Resources
problem: Plasma state reconstruction at DIII-D requires 62 minutes on local resources, limiting the ability to make informed experimental decisions between successive pulses.
motivation: Reducing reconstruction time to under 12 minutes enables real-time physics-informed decisions on experimental configuration between pulses during fusion facility operations.
method: The OMFIT CAKE workflow was automated to distribute plasma state reconstruction computations across DIII-D local resources and the Perlmutter supercomputer at NERSC via the DOE Integrated Research Infrastructure (IRI). The hybrid system orchestrates task scheduling and data movement to parallelize reconstruction and provide results within the inter-pulse window.
key_novelty: Integrating a physics facility's reconstruction workflow with remote leadership-class computing through DOE IRI achieves 5.6x speedup, enabling near-real-time decision support during experiments.
contributions: Automated distributed OMFIT CAKE workflow across DIII-D and NERSC resources via IRI
5.6x wall-clock time reduction for plasma state reconstruction (62 to 11 minutes)
Demonstrated real-time decision capability within inter-pulse windows
Integrated pipeline supporting downstream physics analyses including microturbulence classification
primary_theme: Real-time plasma reconstruction via remote supercomputing
